To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we demonstrate a giant anisotropic magnetoreistance in canted antferromagnet Sr2I2O4.
we have demonstrated a giant AMR in canted AFM Sr2 IrO4 and a bistable nonvolatile resistance states that can be controlled by a small external magnetic field.

the giant AMR and nonvolatile memory states in a simple resistor made of AFM canted antiferomagnet Sr2Ir1-xGaxO4 are realized by the combination of the atomic scale giant-MRs-like effect and magnetocystalline anistropy energy, which are not accessed earlier.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of materials and devices for spintronics applications.
the development of a new class of antiferromagnet-based memory devices.
the study of the magnetoresistance (MR) effect in the canted antiferro-magnetic (CAFM) compound Sr2IrO 4.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the giant AMR effect in canted AFM Sr2 IrO4 is attributed to the combination of the atomic scale giant-MOR-like effect with the magnetocrystallist anisotropy, and the bistable non-volatile memory states can be switched in situ without the inconvenient heat assisted procedure, and are robustly preserved even in zero magnetic field.
the AMR of Sr2IrO 4 is a consequence of both the atomic scale giant-MRs and the MCA.
the AMR of Sr2IrO 4 can be enhanced up to ~160% by combining a giant-MR-like atomic effect and magnetocrystal anisotropy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated the remarkably enhanced AMR as giant as ~150% in a simple AFM resistor structure made of Sr2IrO _{4} without auxiliary reference layer, which is the first report in the field of AFM-spintronic.

we have demonstrated the remarkably enhanced AMR in a simple resistor made of AFM material without auxiliary reference layer, and the underlying mechanism is an indispensable combination between the atomic scale giant-MOKE-like effect and the magnetocrystallin anisotropy.

we demonstrate the AFM spin-valve effect in the AFM Sr2O4 by the combination of atomic-scale giant MR-like effect and magnetic anisotropy, and further show that the nonvolatile memory states can be switched in situ without the inconvenient heat assisted procedure.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the giant anisotropic magnetore- sistance (AMR), which is a key component of spintronics, can be realized in a single-layer AFM material without auxiliary reference layer, and can be used to determine the AFM spin structure and to realize the nonvolatile memory.
a giant AMR can be obtained in AFM Sr2IO4, without auxiliary reference layer, by the combination of atomic layer thickness and the magnetocrystallin anisotropy.
the AFM spintronics community can now utilize the AMR as a readout mechanism for AFM orders.
